memory_update.text: For broad Technology work, AI infrastructure chokepoint research should preserve a two-lane funnel: reference leaders provide context, while underfollowed second-order suppliers, materials, distributors, and process-control nodes drive discovery.

High-end AI-server MLCCs and upstream dielectric powders remain the strongest underfollowed Layer 1 lane because the bottleneck appears concentrated in product-grade capability, particle-size/material know-how, and qualification rather than generic capacitor volume.
ABF build-up film and advanced package substrates should remain a distinct AI accelerator chokepoint separate from chip design, foundry capacity, HBM, and networking.

Inspection, metrology, and process-control tools are cross-winner AI infrastructure nodes because rising chip and packaging complexity can increase the value of yield control across multiple customers.

Cybersecurity, cloud software, AI application software, and data-center electrical/thermal infrastructure need separate node-expansion passes before the Technology theme universe can be considered balanced across software and physical infrastructure.

Layer 2 must upgrade Substack-derived hypotheses to primary-source evidence from filings, annual reports, company presentations, product documentation, earnings transcripts, standards, import/export data, and customer disclosures.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe for the broad Technology theme, with emphasis on AI infrastructure supply-chain chokepoints rather than obvious mega-cap demand anchors. The highest-priority initial universe clusters around high-end AI-server MLCCs, upstream MLCC dielectric powders, ABF/build-up film and advanced package substrates, semiconductor process control, and second-order distribution or supply-chain coordination signals. This is a research-prioritization universe only, not a buy/sell list. Several names are intentionally retained as hypotheses because they sit one or two steps away from obvious AI demand and have clear hidden signals to verify in later layers.
